text:
maria: Quick heads-up — replay vs synth run comparing kernel vA->vB. At high batch caps (batch_cap=256, max_delay=30ms) we see a 9-12% p50 regression and intermittent tail spikes concentrated on tenants with high KV-cache miss rates.

aj: What's the exact command you used?

maria: I used the harness below (replay trace from last week):
```
./replay_harness --trace replay_2026-03-18.json \
  --kernels vA,vB \
  --batch-cap 256 \
  --max-delay-ms 30 \
  --kv-miss-sim=0.6 \
  --concurrency 200
```

tom: Are these runs with prefix cache warm? The tenants that show regressions are the ones we previously flagged as cold.

sophia: I ran a small repro locally. When a batch contains requests that require switching kernels mid-batch we trigger a compile path which adds ~7-10ms per swap. Repro logs below:
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:01Z] kernel_swap: vA->vB compile_start
[2026-03-18T15:12:01Z] compile_end: 7.9ms
[2026-03-18T15:12:01Z] request 3245 latency +9.2ms
```

aj: That matches my hypothesis: kernel selection + compile churn + large batches = bad combo. Two quick mitigations to try: 1) enforce kernel affinity so a batch doesn't mix kernels, 2) reduce batch_cap (try 128) for mixed-tenant traffic.

sophia: Also, KV cache eviction policy is amplifying the problem: multi-tenant interleaving pushes cold keys out more often, increasing miss rate. We should test isolation (per-tenant warmup) vs global cache.

maria: Agreed. Plan for controlled experiments:
A) baseline: no affinity, batch_cap=256, kv-miss-sim=0.6
B) kernel-affinity=on, batch_cap=256
C) kernel-affinity=on, batch_cap=128, kv-warmup enabled
I'll run each for 30m and upload p50/p95/p99, compile-rate/min, and kvcache hit-rate per-tenant.

tom: Add one more: D) disabled just-in-time kernel compilation (if possible) to measure pure latency cost vs compile. Also annotate autoscaler events — if a GPU rebind happens it skews tail.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T15:20:00Z started: replay-harness v2 -> nodeset-playbook (CI: #4821) :rocket:

maria: Kicking off A now. I'll post plots and the replay link when done. If anyone wants to join the run: grab a seat on the ephemeral dashboard (link will be up).

aj: When you post plots, include per-tenant QPS and batch-size distribution. That will show whether big batches are dominated by a few tenants.

sophia: For analysis, compute a "compile-impact" metric: sum(compile_time for batch)/num_requests_in_batches_with_swap. That isolates compile cost.

maria: Good idea — adding that metric. ETA for first results ~40m.

tom: Thanks — ping us on results. If affinity reduces swaps but increases latency due to smaller effective batch diversity, we'll need to tune tradeoffs.

maria: noted. Will include unit cost delta too (tokens/sec and GPU-ms).
